title: Plan your week: big rocks first, and a kind no

say: Plan your week: big rocks first, and a kind no.
This is the video for Module 2, Planning and Prioritising.
When everything feels like it must be done today, you need a quick way to decide what comes first. Ask two questions of every task.
First, is it urgent? Does it need attention now, with a real consequence if it waits? An order due at 4 pm today, or a child with a high fever.

panel.heading: Urgent things shout, important things whisper
items: Urgent: needs attention now or very soon
Important: serves your goals and wellbeing
Plan important tasks before they become urgent

say: Second, is it important? Does it move you towards your goals, or protect your family's health, income or wellbeing? Saving for school fees, checking your business records, rest.

panel.heading: Urgent things shout, important things whisper
items: Urgent: needs attention now or very soon
Important: serves your goals and wellbeing
Plan important tasks before they become urgent

say: Urgent things shout. Important things often whisper, and they are never urgent until it is too late, like servicing the generator.

panel.heading: Urgent things shout, important things whisper
items: Urgent: needs attention now or very soon
Important: serves your goals and wellbeing
Plan important tasks before they become urgent

say: The urgent-important matrix gives you four boxes. Box 1 is urgent and important. Do it now, yourself. A leaking pipe, rent due tomorrow.

panel.heading: Four boxes, four actions
items: 1. Urgent and important: do it now
3. Urgent, not important: delegate or batch

say: Box 2 is important but not urgent. Give it a day and a time. Planning, savings, learning, a health check.
This is the key box. Service the generator on a planned Saturday, and it does not break down the night before an exam.

panel.heading: Four boxes, four actions
items: 1. Urgent and important: do it now
3. Urgent, not important: delegate or batch

say: Box 3 is urgent but not important to you. Delegate it, shorten it or batch it. Most calls and messages sit here.
When you delegate, say what, by when, and what done looks like. Then check once, kindly, and trust the person.

panel.heading: Four boxes, four actions
items: 1. Urgent and important: do it now
3. Urgent, not important: delegate or batch

say: Box 4 is neither. Endless scrolling, chain messages, long gossip. Drop it or limit it.
The common mistake is putting everything in box 1. Ask honestly: what happens if this waits until tomorrow?

panel.heading: Four boxes, four actions
items: 1. Urgent and important: do it now
3. Urgent, not important: delegate or batch

say: Choose a fixed time each week, for example Sunday evening. Give each step about 5 minutes.
Step one. Review last week: what got done, what did not, and why.

panel.heading: Your weekly planning session
items: Write fixed commitments on the days

say: Step two. Write your fixed commitments on the days. Work hours, school events, appointments, worship, deliveries.

panel.heading: Your weekly planning session
items: Write fixed commitments on the days

say: Step three. Choose your big rocks, the three to five most important tasks for the week, mostly from box 2.

panel.heading: Your weekly planning session
items: Write fixed commitments on the days

say: Step four. Give each big rock a day and a time, in your best-energy hours.
Think of a jar. Pour in sand first and the big rocks do not fit. Put the rocks in first and the sand settles around them.

panel.heading: Your weekly planning session
items: Write fixed commitments on the days
panel.rule: Big rocks go in first. Small tasks always find space.

say: Step five, add your home rhythm: market day, laundry day, cooking days. And step six, leave at least one free hour on most days for the unexpected.

panel.heading: Your weekly planning session
items: Write fixed commitments on the days
panel.rule: Big rocks go in first. Small tasks always find space.

say: For example, Aisha is a nurse on day shifts in Kano who sells perfume oils on WhatsApp. On Sunday evening she writes her shifts, a PTA meeting and a family visit on the days.

panel.heading: Aisha plans her week
items: Fixed: four shifts, PTA meeting, family visit
Eye test and restock on Wednesday, her day off
Market Saturday 8 am, stews on Sunday

say: She places her big rocks. Her daughter's eye test and restocking go on Wednesday, her day off. The catalogue post goes on Thursday at 7 pm.

panel.heading: Aisha plans her week
items: Fixed: four shifts, PTA meeting, family visit
Eye test and restock on Wednesday, her day off
Market Saturday 8 am, stews on Sunday

say: Then home rhythm, market on Saturday at 8 am and two stews cooked and frozen on Sunday. And she leaves Friday evening free.
When her shift runs late on Friday, nothing important is lost. All four big rocks were done by Thursday night.

panel.heading: Aisha plans her week
items: Fixed: four shifts, PTA meeting, family visit

Market Saturday 8 am, stews on Sunday

say: Goals help you choose your big rocks. But vague goals like save more rarely happen.

panel.heading: From a wish to a goal

say: A SMART goal is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound. Save approximately 150,000 naira for my son's next school fees by 1 September, putting aside 15,000 naira every week.
Now you can check every week whether you are on track.

panel.heading: From a wish to a goal

say: Your plan will be tested by requests. The most powerful tool is the pause. Say: let me check my week and get back to you this evening.

panel.heading: Pause before you answer
items: Pause: let me check my week
Ask: is it important to me?
Choose yes, a smaller yes, or no

say: Then check your plan and ask what you would give up.

panel.heading: Pause before you answer
items: Pause: let me check my week
Ask: is it important to me?
Choose yes, a smaller yes, or no

say: For example, Patience's aunt asked for her whole Saturday, but she had tailoring orders due on Monday. Patience offered a smaller yes, 2 hours on Saturday morning.
A kind no has a warm opening, a clear answer and often an alternative. Long explanations invite argument.

panel.heading: Pause before you answer
items: Pause: let me check my week
Ask: is it important to me?
Choose yes, a smaller yes, or no
panel.rule: Every yes is also a no to something in your 168 hours.

say: Scams use urgency to stop you thinking. A message says a relative is in trouble, or you must pay a fee to receive a prize.
Pause. Call the person directly on a number you already know. And never share your bank PIN or one-time password with anyone.

panel.heading: When a message says send money now
items: Call the person on a number you know
Never share your bank PIN or OTP

say: Now try it. Sort your real list, plan next week, write one SMART goal, and practise the pause. Continue with the lessons below.

panel.heading: Your practice tasks
items: Sort your real list into four boxes
Write one SMART goal with steps
Practise the pause for a week
